At least five Israeli-backed Palestinian militias are operating out of
compounds in areas under Israeli military control across the Gaza Strip,
according to satellite imagery and videos published online. Since the so-
called ceasefire went into effect nearly a year ago, these compounds have been
upgraded and expanded in size and sophistication, according to a preliminary
analysis by Forensic Architecture. Many of these upgrades resemble Israeli
military infrastructure, with berms, barracks, fences, and buildings. At least
one compound in East Rafah includes new shops, classrooms, and a playground.

While there have been some splinter groups and defections, the five main
Israel-backed Palestinian militias are known as:

  * Northern forces/Popular Army in Beit Lahia, led by Ashraf Al-Mansi

  * Popular Defense Forces in Shujaieya, east of Gaza City, led by Rami Halas

  * Free Homeland Forces in central/eastern Gaza near Deir al-Balah, led by Shawqi Abu Nasira

  * Counter-Terrorism Strike Force in southeastern Khan Younis, led by Hussam al-Astal

  * Popular Forces/Counter-Terrorism Service in East Rafah, led by Ghassan Al-Duhaini

Many of the militia leaders who rose to power in collaboration with Israel
during the genocide in Gaza are former gang leaders with a history of criminal
activity, were associated with jihadi groups, or are former Palestinian
Authority security forces that were all sidelined after Hamas gained control
of the enclave in 2007.

"These militias are not just Israel-backed. These militias are Israel-
created," Muhammad Shehada, a writer and analyst from Gaza and a visiting
fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations, told Drop Site News. "The
IDF and the Shin Bet [Israel's domestic intelligence service] were the ones
that recruited, funded, trained, provided shelter, accommodation, food, and so
on to these gangs, brought them together, and designated each one of them a
very specific turf that they operate in."

Four of the five compounds where the militias are based are located very close
to the "yellow line"--the demarcation of Israel's line of control--and all are
close to Israeli military bases. Israel has established nearly 40 military
bases in areas across Gaza east of the yellow line. One militia compound
located in east Khan Younis, right on the yellow line, is less than one
kilometer from two Israeli military bases.

Initially, Israel's primary objective for the gangs was to systematically loot
aid coming into Gaza, starting around May 2024, as Israeli troops stood by and
did not intervene. "That was the first use that Israel had for them: loot aid
systematically while giving Israel plausible deniability," Shehada said. "They
eventually dressed them up in police uniforms with Palestinian logos on to
pretend that they were some sort of a legitimate authority with a propaganda
psyop operation behind them." He added, "They suddenly became an organized
militia instead of just bandits."

Militia members are granted relative freedom of movement by the Israeli
military and privileged access to resources, such as weapons and medical
treatment within Israel. Militias have also conducted armed raids and
[attacks](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/israel-abu-nasira-militia-attack-
maghazi-camp-gaza?utm_source=publication-search) on Palestinians living near
the yellow line in coordination with the Israeli military, who have backed
them up with artillery and aerial support.

At least one compound in East Rafah includes new shops, classrooms, and a
playground. A [video](https://www.facebook.com/reel/942440391861102) published
on April 2, 2026 shows the inside of a classroom equipped with air
conditioning inside the compound of the Counter-Terrorism Service militia. In
the video, Ghassan Al-Duhaini--who took over as commander of the Popular
Forces militia, also known as the Counter-Terrorism Service, following the
killing of its former leader Yasser Abu Shabbab--is seen touring a classroom
as schoolchildren receive educational instruction. These compounds are not
open to all Palestinians but are used for a select few, including the families
of those affiliated with the militias.

Since the so-called ceasefire went into effect nearly a year ago, Israel has
been [fortifying](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/gaza-israel-earth-berms-
military-bases-ceasefire) military bases in the eastern part of the territory
it controls and constructing a physical barrier walling off Palestinians from
most of the Gaza Strip. In parallel, the compounds for the Israel-backed
Palestinian militias have also been upgraded and fortified, including using
Israeli construction materials such as T walls (a T-shaped structural barrier
or wall panel).

The ongoing construction and fortification of the Israeli military bases and
Palestinian militia compounds comes despite a complete lack of reconstruction
in the western part of Gaza, where nearly all Palestinians in Gaza have been
corralled. Israel has not allowed reconstruction materials and equipment into
Gaza over the past year, in violation of the ceasefire agreement. Hundreds of
thousands of Palestinians are living in dilapidated tent encampments or
seeking shelter in buildings badly damaged by the Israeli assault that are at
risk of collapse. Last week, in just the latest incident, at least 21
Palestinians, including 12 children, were killed and 45 others injured when a
residential building collapsed in Gaza City. More than 100 people, including
50 children, are estimated to have been sheltering in the building.

"The thing to know about these gangs is that their structures are entirely
unsustainable," Shehada said. "They have been artificially created by the
Israeli government, the army, the Shin Bet--and the only thing that binds them
together is basically the bribes that they receive from the IDF, the
protection that they receive from the IDF, the territory that they are allowed
to live in, with upgraded privileges compared to the rest of the population in
western Gaza. If these things disappear, the gangs will disintegrate."

## The Forensic Architecture Analysis

### Militia compounds

In Gaza, at least five Palestinian militias are operating in the area under
Israeli military control. These are Palestinian armed groups backed by Israel,
who provide them with resources and freedom of movement.

Their compounds are located in the Israeli-controlled area, between military
bases.

### Since the ceasefire, militia compounds have developed

Another militia compound is located near an Israeli military base in east
Rafah. This group, known as the Counter-Terrorism Service, existed before the
ceasefire, but since the ceasefire its presence has grown.

While Israel has continued to demolish buildings nearby, new structures have
been added to the compound. Videos show it has new shops, classrooms, and a
playground--facilities that are accessible only to militia members and their
families.

Israel has allowed the militias to use large machinery and Israeli materials.
